question: A product page is read 500 times for every write and the database CPU is at 90%. What is the first change you should make?
context: Latency is dominated by the same SELECT for popular products. Prices change a few times a day and a minute of staleness is acceptable.

options.label: Shard the database by product id
options.why: Sharding solves write or data-volume limits and costs a lot of complexity. The problem here is repeated identical reads, which a cache removes almost for free.

options.label: Add Redis with Cache Aside and a 60-second TTL
options.why: Read-heavy, repeated, staleness-tolerant data is the textbook cache case. Cache Aside is low risk (the app falls back to the database) and the TTL bounds staleness to the accepted minute.

options.label: Move to microservices
options.why: Splitting services does nothing for a hot read path; every service would still hit the same database.

options.label: Switch to MongoDB
options.why: Changing the database engine does not change the access pattern. The same 500:1 reads would land on the new store.
